Assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Policy stance: The statement is hawkish—“ongoing increases” to reach a “sufficiently restrictive” stance, continued QT ($60B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS), and money-market settings (IORB 4.65%, ON RRP 4.55%) that reinforce tight conditions.
- SLOOS signal: Banks report broad tightening of lending standards for C&I and CRE loans, with weaker demand across nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, and multifamily. Lenders also cite decreased financing needs for plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, and A/R; foreign banks report weaker C&I demand as well. This points to a meaningful contraction in bank credit supply and softer credit demand.
- Policy transmission: The SLOOS tightening amplifies the restrictiveness of current policy via the bank credit channel, complementing higher market rates and QT. This strengthens the case for the Committee’s emphasis on cumulative tightening and long/variable lags.
- Risk balance: While inflation remains elevated, SLOOS evidence of tighter credit and weaker demand tilts risks more toward growth and financial conditions than the headline statement alone suggests.
- Net: Hawkish baseline tempered by SLOOS-driven credit headwinds—overall mildly hawkish rather than firmly so.
